Explanation: Chromosome containing the variant, such as 1, X, or MT.
1-based genomic coordinate in GRCh38
Reference and alternate alleles, shown as reference>alternate (for example, A>G).
dbSNP identifier for the variant; blank when no identifier is available.
Gene selected for the winning scoring hypothesis (Scored_gene). The | CASE marker means this selected gene is listed in the case context; it does not by itself establish a diagnosis.

Indicates whether the variant is also in secondary-finding gene; may include the associated condition and inheritance model. If TRUE it dosent neccesarly means its reportable, this depnds on pathgenity and inheritence fit.
Transcripts belonging to Scored_gene. The selected Scored_transcript is highlighted in blue, and MANE transcripts are bold.
Biological type of the Scored_gene transcript, such as protein_coding.
Predicted sequence consequences for Scored_gene transcripts, such as missense_variant or intron_variant.
HGVS coding (c.) and protein (p.) descriptions for the variant on Scored_gene transcripts.
Variant location in the gene or transcript, such as EXON 2/3, INTRON, or UPSTREAM.
Regulatory annotations associated with the variant from ENCODE and ensembel, such as promoter or enhancer context.
Known protein domains for Scored_gene transcripts, such as Pfam, PANTHER, or PROSITE domains.
Combined sample genotype and read support: GT | alternate reads/total depth | VAF (for example, 0/1 | 9/20 | 0.45).

Global gnomAD joint allele frequency for nuclear variants; MT rows use mitochondrial AF. Nuclear missing AF displays as 0. Rarity scoring also uses population-group maximum AF, retained in the scored table.
Nuclear counts: heterozygotes | homozygotes; X rows also include hemizygotes. MT rows instead show labelled homoplasmic_AF and heteroplasmic_AF values when available.
Candidate inheritance model such as AD, AR_homozygous, AR_compound_heterozygous, X_linked, Mosaic, or Mitochondrial
ClinVar classification and associated condition, when available.
CADD PHRED score. Below 10 is low; 20 or higher ranks among the top 1 percent, and 30 or higher among the top 0.1 percent of possible single nucleotide substitutions by predicted deleteriousness.

Combines phyloP and phastCons conservation. phyloP below 0 suggests accelerated evolution; values near 0 indicate little conservation, 1 or higher stronger conservation, and 2.5 or higher the top scoring range. phastCons ranges from 0 to 1; values near 0 indicate low conservation, around 0.45 moderate conservation, and 0.75 or higher the top scoring range.

Gene-level loss-of-function observed/expected upper-bound fraction for Scored_gene. Below 0.35 indicates strong constraint; 0.35 to 0.90 indicates intermediate constraint; above 0.90 indicates weaker constraint.

Gene-level missense constraint for Scored_gene, shown as observed/expected (O/E) and Z score. O/E near 1 is close to expectation; lower O/E indicates greater depletion of missense mutations. Z below 0 indicates little or no depletion; Z of 3 or higher indicates strong depletion.

Annotation-supported routes across selected-gene transcripts, such as MISSENSE, LOF, SPLICE, INFRAME and REGULATORY. The selected scoring route is first and bold; COMMON-only evidence has no named route here.

Route annotation evidence: MISSENSE: REVEL, AlphaMissense and available SIFT; SPLICE: SpliceAI and transcript splice distance; LOF: LOFTEE/NMD; INFRAME: functional evidence; REGULATORY: annotations/ReMM. Protein domains (MISSENSE/INFRAME), LOEUF and MANE (LOF), and transcript TSS distance (REGULATORY) also contribute to scoring but are not all repeated here. This is evidence text, not a complete numerical breakdown.

Absolute distance in bases to the nearest splice site among Stage 3 transcripts, followed by transcript ID. Shown only when the distance is <50 bases and the transcript belongs to the selected gene; otherwise blank.

Absolute distance in bases to the nearest transcription start site among Stage 3 transcripts, followed by transcript ID. The nearest transcript may belong to a different gene from Scored_gene; scoring uses transcript-specific TSS evidence.
Known disease associations for Scored_gene, with evidence strength when available.
Reported inheritance pattern and disease mechanism for conditions associated with Scored_gene.
Scored_gene ClinVar summary with the fraction and count of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, plus counts by consequence.
Phenotype terms associated with diseases linked to Scored_gene.
Patient HPO terms matched to selected-gene disease phenotypes by exact identity or an HPO ancestor/descendant relationship; shown as patient term <-> disease term.
Summary of reviewed literature evidence for the gene or disease, including human cases and functional or animal studies when available.
Selected publication references relevant to the candidate gene or disease, such as PMID, year, title, and DOI.
Observed evidence weight for the selected transcript and route, divided by 100 (0-1). Missing-evidence defaults and the ClinVar adjustment do not add coverage; this is not a probability.

0-100 pathogenicity score for the winning transcript and route: CADD, conservation, route evidence and main ClinVar adjustment. Missing evidence may receive neutral defaults; MT evaluation is partial.

0-100 fit to the case's expected inheritance. Exact matches score 100, except compound-heterozygous matches score 80 because phase is unconfirmed. Missing context/category scores 50; an approved alternative-gene AD fallback against expected AR can score 25. Gene-disease inheritance fit is assessed separately.
0-100 selected-gene evidence score combining GenCC association strength, gene-disease inheritance compatibility, ClinVar consequence/count/fraction evidence and literature support.

0-100 hierarchical case relevance: a case-gene or disease-name match scores 100; otherwise broad disease-domain and HPO matches are considered with documented defaults. These signals are not simply added.

0-100 rarity under the selected inheritance model, using the higher of global and population-group maximum AF plus relevant het/hom/X-hemi counts. Compound alleles use het and hom support. MT rarity is unavailable and uses the existing 50/100 default.

Mean of the two selected compound partners' individual Final_score values. Qualifying pair scores guide pair/gene ranking; individual Final_score remains unchanged. Workbook order also prioritises case genes and groups by gene. This field appears only on sheets with compound-pair columns.

Selected reciprocal compound partner, in chromosome:position|REF>ALT format. Blank when no pair is selected, including alternative-gene AD fallbacks. Present only on sheets with compound-pair columns.

Weighted 0-100 candidate score: 30% pathogenicity + 20% inheritance + 25% gene-disease evidence + 15% case relevance + 10% rarity. Missing-evidence defaults can contribute; the score is not a probability of diagnosis.
